newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish right takes lead in opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: Polish right takes lead in opinion poll.

text.p: Poland's opposition rightist bloc led by the Solidarity trade union took the lead in February from the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) in an opinion polls published on Thursday by the independent Demoskop institute.
The poll showed the bloc, called the Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS), would get 24 percent of the vote if parliamentary elections were held next week, up from 21 percent in January.
The rating of the SLD, the stronger party in the four-year-old ruling leftist coalition, had remained flat at 23 percent since January.
The AWS was created in mid-1996, uniting more than 30 small, splintered right-wing groups around the Solidarity union, which toppled the communist system in 1989.
Poland's parliamentary elections are due around September.
The co-ruling Peasant Party (PSL), rated third in the poll, saw its support shrinking to 14 percent in February from 17 percent a month earlier.
The biggest parliamentary opposition party, the Union for Freedom (UW), kept its fourth position, favoured by 11 percent of voters both in January and February.
The Demoskop poll, carried out between February 6 and 11, had a three percent error margin.
